method: Fabs and back-end sites in Israel, Singapore, Germany, Costa Rica and Vietnam (including one paused project), Spain's PERTE Chip and the Philippines' CREATE MORE Act, and equipment models for makers with no models (Park Systems, HPSP, Beneq, Oxford Instruments, Thermo Fisher, KCTech), from company releases, government pages, product pages and industry news located by web search; titles and search-result summaries.

pr.tech: Automated atomic force microscope: automatic defect review from laser-scattering defect maps, auto tip exchange, robot wafer handling (EFEM / FOUP), long-range sliding stage for CMP profiling (per Park Systems)
pr.app: Bare-wafer defect review; CMP dishing, erosion and edge-over-erosion; sub-angstrom roughness
pr.note: Batch 18: from Park Systems product pages; an NX-Wafer Plus variant adds edge profiling and SECS/GEM. Accuracy figures are company claims.

pr.tech: High-pressure anneal process (HPAP) tool combining a batch furnace with high-pressure processing up to 25 atm in various ambients; lowers thermal budget (per HPSP)
pr.app: High-pressure hydrogen anneal to wet oxidation for 14 nm and beyond logic, 3D NAND and CIS
pr.note: Batch 18: from HPSP's SEMI member profile and imec JDP release summaries; HPSP describes itself as first to commercialise high-pressure hydrogen annealing.

pr.tech: 300 mm ALD cluster tool with thermal batch ALD (up to 25 wafers, up to 420 °C) and single-wafer plasma ALD (up to 350 °C); up to 3 process modules plus a preheater; SECS/GEM (per Beneq)
pr.app: CMOS image sensors, power devices, micro-OLED / microLED, advanced packaging
pr.note: Batch 18: launched Dec 2021 (per SEMI-hosted release); specifications from the Beneq brochure summary.

pr.tech: Stand-alone thermal ALD batch tool: 150 mm x 50 or 100 mm x 75 wafers, 25–420 °C, no plasma (per Beneq)
pr.app: Compound semiconductors (GaAs, GaN, InP RF ICs), LEDs, VCSELs, photodetectors, MEMS

pr.tech: Inductively coupled plasma reactive-ion etch with a high-density plasma source; electrode range typically -150 °C to +400 °C; configurations include deep-silicon Bosch and cryogenic etch (per Oxford Instruments and user facilities)
pr.app: Volume VCSEL production, III-V etch, microLEDs, quantum devices (NbN, Ta), metalenses
pr.note: Batch 18: from the Oxford Instruments product page; wafer size and gases vary by installation.

pr.tech: 300 mm full-wafer focused ion beam / SEM for TEM sample preparation; optional automated FOUP loader for in-fab use; KLARF-based defect navigation with AutoTEM 5 recipes (per Thermo Fisher)
pr.app: In-fab TEM lamella preparation and defect root-cause analysis at sub-5 nm and GAA nodes, without cleaving wafers
pr.note: Batch 18: filed under e-beam inspection because the taxonomy has no failure-analysis category; from Thermo Fisher product and blog summaries.

pr.tech: CMP system, KCTech's flagship; about 30 % efficiency gain over previous models (per company interview)
pr.app: CMP for advanced nodes (2 nm-class, per interview), with in-house ceria slurry
pr.note: Batch 18: named in a 2026 interview with KCTech's vice chairman; specifications not published in reviewed sources.

fa.name: Intel Fab 38, Kiryat Gat (Israel)
fa.scheme: Israeli government grant of $3.25 billion (Dec 2023), cancelled by the Ministry of Finance in July 2026 (per coverage)
fa.notes: Expansion frozen since 2024. The first building is constructed with utilities installed but not equipped; the second is a concrete shell; contractor headcount fell from about 5,500 to 2,000 (per Globes). An unconfirmed Aug 2026 report of renewed planning is not recorded. Originally planned to come online in 2028.

fa.name: GlobalFoundries Singapore 300 mm expansion fab, Woodlands
partners: Singapore Economic Development Board and customers (co-investors)

invest.label: US$4 billion (about S$5 billion), co-invested with EDB and customers

fa.capacity: Adds 450,000 300 mm wafers a year, raising GF Singapore to about 1.5 million a year (per EDB)
fa.notes: Broke ground in 2021 as part of a $6 billion global expansion; officially opened 12 Sept 2023, with a 23,000 m² cleanroom. The 'Fab 7H' label is not used in the reviewed sources.

fa.name: Bosch 300 mm wafer fab, Dresden
fa.scheme: Support from the German federal government under the first IPCEI on Microelectronics (2018), per Bosch

invest.label: About €1 billion, Bosch's largest single investment (per Bosch)

fa.capacity: About 31,000 chips per 300 mm wafer (per Bosch)
fa.technology: Automotive ICs and power semiconductors; MEMS on 300 mm planned for series production in 2027
fa.notes: Groundbreaking in spring 2018; first wafers in Jan 2021; opened 7 Jun 2021, with full-scale production from Jul 2021 (per Bosch).

fa.name: Intel assembly and test plant, Belén (Costa Rica)

invest.label: US$600 million (raised from US$350 million in Jul 2021)

fa.notes: Intel restarted assembly and test in Costa Rica with a 26,000 m² plant on its Belén campus; operations began in 2021 with a first export (per CINDE). A 2025 expansion was not found in reviewed sources.

fa.name: Hana Micron Vina second plant, Van Trung (Bac Giang)

invest.label: Nearly US$600 million invested in Bac Giang (per coverage); target over US$1 billion by 2025

fa.technology: Packaging and test; 2.5D packaging for HBM in development (per coverage)
fa.notes: Second Bac Giang factory, inaugurated Sept 2023. Sources differ on when the first phase started (2020 or 2022). Whether the US$1 billion target was met by 2025 is not confirmed in reviewed sources.

pg.name: Spain PERTE Chip (Strategic Project for Microelectronics and Semiconductors)

facts.label: Approved
facts.value: 24 May 2022 by the Council of Ministers

facts.label: Budget
facts.value: €12.25 billion of public investment by 2027, financed from EU Recovery Plan funds

facts.label: Scope
facts.value: Four axes: R&D, chip design, manufacturing plants and industry; a Chip Fund initially endowed with €200 million for start-ups and scale-ups

facts.label: Example round
facts.value: Jan 2025 tender: seven projects selected, €40.6 million of grants (per GTAI)

facts.label: Incentives
facts.value: 20 % corporate income tax under the Enhanced Deductions Regime; power-expense deduction raised from 50 % to 100 %; incentive period up to 27 years (from 17)

facts.label: Semiconductors
facts.value: No semiconductor-specific provision; semiconductor firms fall under the general regime (per PIDS)
